AUTHOR: Catalán
TITLE: AI-powered underwater imaging reveals multiscale occurrence and volume-based abundance patterns in coastal fishes
REGION: Port d'Andratx harbour entrance, Mallorca, western Mediterranean (Spain)
SPECIES: 16 species/genera (Diplodus sargus, D. vulgaris, Chromis chromis, Oblada melanura, Seriola dumerili, Sparus aurata, Coris julis, etc.) + generic 'fish'
DATA: Own cabled fixed-camera time series 2016-2024 (442,000 images; 81,284 after filtering)
V_EV: Sec. 2.2.1: classifier 'removed images that were too dark (near night-time), severely blurred or turbid'; 'No further correction for detection efficiency was applied'
D_EV: no statement found (model 'trained on a curated and annotated dataset' described in Catalán et al. 2023; no split reported)
R_EV: Sec. 2.1: images 'collected from a fixed cabled underwater camera installed at 8 m depth' (single site; no external test reported)
C_EV: Sec. 4.4: 'a single trained model and fixed detection threshold were applied' (threshold value not reported)
E_EV: Abstract/Sec. 2.3: 'daily occurrence (presence-absence)' and 'daylight hourly fish density standardized by an estimated sampled water volume (individuals m-3 h-1)'; nine-year trends
ARCH: Deep-learning image-quality filter + Multiscale Retinex + YOLOv8 detector/classifier
METR: mAP@0.5 (0.8), per-class AP; GLMMs and hurdle models of occurrence/density
NOTE: Detector previously described in Catalán et al. 2023; mAP 0.8 reported without split details (D NR). Poor-visibility (dark, blurred, turbid) images excluded by automatic filter without measuring visibility -> V_ALL=N per policy P1 even though depth (8 m), irradiance and camera-wreck distance are reported. Ecological models (binomial GLMM, hurdle) do not correct for detection -> E3=없음 (paper: 'No further correction for detection efficiency was applied'). No comparison to human or independent counts.
